slots.workflow-matrix/title: A traceable case journey can reduce ambiguity without merging systems
slots.workflow-matrix/matrix-takeaway/text: Journey details and operating assumptions require discovery validation.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-0: Keep the entry channel, service queue and processing responsibilities visible as separate participants. Confirm where transaction state originates and who can change it.
Represent requester portal, shared operations queue, and three downstream processing systems as distinct participants.
Confirm business and system owners; trace where transaction state is created and changed.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-1: Check completeness at entry and route missing information back to the requester with a clear reason. Keep the alternate route visible so the transition does not depend on an unproven interface.
Show intake validation and missing-information return path while alternate intake remains available during transition.
Business owner confirms required information, alternate intake and the return-path decision.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-2: A case must have an accountable business owner, a service queue and a known escalation route. Capture the accountable owner and queue at the decision point; record why a case is reassigned.
Assign business owner, service queue, and escalation route at each case state; capture decision and reassignment reasons.
Record state transitions, decision rationale and reassignment reasons in the case history.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-3: Preserve transaction ownership in existing processing systems until an explicit migration decision.

Use the consistent case identifier to link status, access, processing events, and audit history. The case identifier and event trace are proposed design responsibilities, not a committed vendor or platform selection.
Architecture and control owners define the identifier, access boundaries and auditable event linkage.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-4: Separate the exception reason from the case state so operational action and genuine new demand remain distinguishable.

Show technical failure, waiting decision, incomplete intake, and genuine demand as distinct exception categories. Tie each exception category to an explicit next action, escalation owner, and evidence needed to resume processing.
Record the exception reason, recovery owner and decision required to resume processing.
slots.slide/takeaway: A single case identifier and explicit state ownership connect intake, decisions, processing, and recovery.
